[Project overview]{.eyebrow}

::: {.lead}
Sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 genomes became the key technology for analyzing the
spread of viral lineages, including detection of variants of concern.
:::

The lab invested significant effort in helping the State of Alaska respond to
the pandemic through a collaboration led by Alaska INBRE called the Alaska
SARS-CoV-2 Sequencing Consortium. We coauthored and then led NIH supplement
proposals that funded increased sequencing capacity and supported research into
the spread of variants of concern across urban and rural communities in Alaska.

That funding produced two papers describing founder events for specific
sublineages during the Alpha and Omicron waves. Alongside the sequencing work,
we collaborated on modeling COVID-19 disease dynamics in Alaska with NIH
support, and joined a nationwide network of IDeA state researchers working on
SARS-CoV-2.

The lab also analyzed sequencing data weekly and maintained a dynamic
[Alaska Coronavirus Variants Dashboard](https://akvariants.github.io/) linked
directly from the Alaska Department of Health COVID-19 dashboard. It was used by
the public and featured in weekly COVID-19 informational sessions, providing
accurate and timely communication about the situation in Alaska.
